title: Counting unit fractions to one
li: We are learning to count unit fractions on a number line to make one whole.
sc: I can explain what a unit fraction is
I can count in unit fractions from 0 to 1, like 1/5, 2/5, 3/5
I can write one whole as a fraction, like 3/3 or 8/8

slides.title: Warm-up: Parts of a whole
items: How many fifths make one whole?
How do we make thirds without folding?
Write three eighths as a fraction.

slides.means: A fraction with 1 on top. It is one equal part of the whole.
slides.example: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 and 1/8 are unit fractions. 3/4 is not.

slides.title: I do: Count quarters to one whole
slides.problem: Count by quarters from 0 to 1 on the number line.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Start at 0. Each jump is one space: 1/4.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Say each landing: one quarter, two quarters, three quarters, four quarters.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Four quarters land on 1. So 4/4 = 1 whole.

slides.notes: Point out that the numerator goes up by 1 each jump while the denominator stays the same, because the size of each part does not change.

slides.title: We do: Count fifths to one whole
slides.problem: Count by fifths from 0 to 1. Write each landing.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: The first jump lands on 1/5. You say the next one.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: One more jump lands on 1. 5/5 = 1 whole.

slides.notes: Students write each label on their whiteboards before you reveal it. Repeat quickly with thirds and eighths if time allows.

slides.title: Fractions keep going past 1

rows.label: Keep counting
rows.text: After 4/4 comes 5/4. That is one quarter more than 1.

rows.label: Big idea
rows.text: Fractions are numbers. They do not stop at 1.

slides.notes: This is a short look ahead. Students do not need to master it today, but it stops the idea that fractions only live between 0 and 1.

slides.title: Turn and talk
slides.prompt: Is 6/6 the same amount as 3/3? Use a number line to explain.
slides.notes: Both are one whole. 6 sixths and 3 thirds both land on 1.

slides.title: Which one?
slides.question: Which fraction is equal to one whole?
why: Wrong: this child sees the 1 on top and thinks 'one whole'. 1/4 is one part of 4.
Right: 4 quarters land on 1, so 4/4 is one whole.
Wrong: this child counted the 3 marks between 0 and 1, not the 4 spaces.
Wrong: this child counted 0 as the first quarter, so went one jump too far.

slides.title: Show me: count to one
questions: Count in fifths from 0 to 1. Write each fraction.
How many jumps of 1/3 from 0 to 1?
Counting in quarters, what comes after 4/4?

slides.title: Activity: Race to One
steps: Play Race to One with a partner.
Roll the die and move along your fraction track.
Say the fraction you land on, like 'three eighths'.
Land exactly on 1 and say the whole as a fraction to win.
Then do your level on the Counting to one whole sheet.
slides.notes: Each pair needs one board, one die and 2 counters. Change tracks each round so students count in different unit fractions.

slides.support: Count quarters and thirds on labelled lines. Write 4/4 = 1 and 3/3 = 1.
slides.core: Count in thirds, fifths and eighths. Fill in missing labels and write each whole as a fraction.
slides.extend: Keep counting past 1. Where do 4/3, 6/4 and 8/4 land? Explain with a number line.

questions: Can a fraction be more than 1? Show us on a number line.
slides.connect: We counted unit fractions from 0 to one whole. Check the success criteria and add to your flip book.
slides.notes: Add the Count to one whole panel. Ask students to write 1 whole three different ways.

teach.text: Count the spaces from 0. Four quarters make one whole: 4/4 = 1.

items.q: What fraction is marked with the dot?

teach.text: A unit fraction has 1 on top. Count unit fractions until you land on one whole.

items.q: How many more jumps of 1/5 from 2/5 to reach 1?
Tom counted the marks and said this line shows fifths. Explain his mistake.
items.answer: There are 5 marks but only 4 spaces, so it shows quarters.
Yes. 6 sixths make one whole, so 6/6 lands on 1.

teach.text: Fractions keep going past 1. 4/4 = 1, so 5/4 is one quarter more than 1.

items.q: Count on in fifths from 3/5. Write the next 4 fractions.
Which of these is more than 1: 7/8, 8/8, 9/8?

items.answer: Halfway between 1 and 2. It is 1 whole and 2 quarters more.

printables.title: Race to One
rules: Each player chooses a track. Both players use the same track each round.
Roll the die. 1, 2 or 3: move 1 space. 4, 5 or 6: move 2 spaces.
Say the fraction you land on out loud. If you say it wrong, move back to where you were.
You must land exactly on 1. If your move is too big, miss that turn.
First to land on 1 says the whole as a fraction (like 5/5) and wins the round.

teacherNotes: The key idea is that the denominator names the size of the part and the numerator counts how many parts, so counting 1/5, 2/5, 3/5 is just like counting objects. Students should say fractions as words while counting. The look past 1 is brief; return to it if students are curious. In Race to One, listen for students who say the mark number instead of the fraction, and check they start counting from 0.
